questions.question: What was the aircraft registration for the last Concorde built?
Which of these is NOT a car model produced by Malaysian car manufacturer Proton?
What iconic car brand, famous for its rounded "Bug" shape, produced a model officially designated the Type 1?
questions.explanation: The Volkswagen Beetle, officially known as the Volkswagen Type 1, is widely regarded as one of the most influential cars of the 20th century. Originally designed in 1930s Germany, it became a global cultural icon and one of the best-selling cars in history. Its distinctive rounded shape earned it the nickname "Bug" or "Beetle" long before Volkswagen officially adopted that name.

questions.question: Between the Space Shuttle's retirement in 2011 and SpaceX Crew Dragon's debut in 2020, Russia's Soyuz spacecraft was the only vehicle capable of ferrying astronauts to and from which orbiting laboratory that has been continuously inhabited since the year 2000?
questions.explanation: From 2011 to 2020, Russia's Soyuz capsule was the sole crewed taxi to the orbiting laboratory that has hosted a continuous human presence since November 2000. This nine-year monopoly ended when SpaceX's Crew Dragon completed its first operational crewed mission in 2020, restoring an American-made path to the station.

questions.question: Felix Wankel famously complained that his elegant "race horse" had been turned into a "plow mare" after discovering that which engineer had redesigned his rotary engine concept into the KKM 57 configuration in 1957?
questions.explanation: Hanns Dieter Paschke redesigned Felix Wankel's rotary engine concept into the KKM 57 configuration in 1957, a change made without Wankel's prior approval. Upon learning of the redesign, Wankel angrily remarked that Paschke had turned his "race horse" into a "plow mare." Despite Wankel's displeasure, Paschke's practical redesign became the foundation for all modern Wankel rotary engines used in automobiles.

questions.question: Union Pacific once contemplated a class of five unbuilt steam locomotives — numbered sequentially after the last production unit — that would have stretched 139 feet 11 5/8 inches long, weighed just under 1.3 million pounds, and been oil-fired rather than coal-fired. What were these proposed 4-8-8-4 locomotives called?
questions.explanation: Union Pacific considered ordering five enlarged Big Boys numbered 4025–4029 that would have surpassed even the already-massive production units in size and weight, and would have burned oil instead of coal. The project never moved beyond the planning stage, making these locomotives among the most intriguing "what-ifs" in American steam history. The Big Boy class itself is already the largest steam locomotive type ever built, so these proposed giants would have been truly extraordinary.
